data.description: The Monument to the People's Heroes is a ten-story obelisk located in the southern part of Tiananmen Square in Beijing, China. Designed by architect Liang Sicheng and his wife Lin Huiyin, the monument stands 37.94 meters tall and is constructed from approximately 17,000 pieces of granite and white marble sourced from Qingdao and Fangshan District. The pedestal features ten large bas-reliefs depicting signi fi cant events in modern Chinese history, including the destruction of opium at Humen, the Jintian Uprising, the Wuchang Uprising, the May 4th Movement, the May 30th Movement, the Nanchang Uprising, the War of Resistance Against Japan, and the Yangtze River Crossing Campaign. An inscription by Mao Zedong on the front reads, 'Eternal glory to the people's heroes!' The monument serves as a focal point for commemorations and has been central to signi fi cant historical events, including the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests.
